hook: $11.99 makes your pillows look like a hotel's

scenes.visual_prompt: Stack of stained, mismatched pillowcases on a bed
scenes.voiceover: If your pillows are still supportive but the cases are stained or yellowing, don't replace the pillows.

scenes.visual_prompt: Package of 4 white queen sham covers, price tag $11.99 visible
scenes.voiceover: A set of four queen pillow covers is $11.99 — that's for all four, not each one.

scenes.visual_prompt: Math graphic: '$60-100 new pillows' crossed out, '$11.99 covers' circled
scenes.voiceover: Buying four new shammed pillows outright runs $60 to $100. This is a fraction of that.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hands zipping a sham cover closed over an existing pillow
scenes.voiceover: Reviewers point to the zipper closure specifically — it's what keeps the fabric from yellowing the way budget cases do.

scenes.visual_prompt: Row of stacked shams behind sleeping pillows on a made bed
scenes.voiceover: A row of stacked shams behind your sleeping pillows is the single visual cue people associate with hotel beds.

scenes.on_screen_text: The full 5-item stack — link in bio
scenes.voiceover: This is the cheapest line item on the whole list. I broke down the rest on the blog.

caption: The cheapest thing on this entire list is also the one that reads most 'hotel' — $11.99 for four sham covers over pillows you already own. Full 5-piece bedding stack breakdown linked in bio.
